# Job Posting API

Feedback

Summarize this article for me


Important

We are currently not accepting new partnerships for LinkedIn's Job Posting API. If you would like to gain access to LinkedIn's Job Posting APIs please request access to [Apply Connect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-connect/apply-connect-overview?view=li-lts-2026-04).

LinkedIn's Job Posting API enables authorized third parties such as clients, ATS systems, and job distributors to post jobs directly to LinkedIn on behalf of customers. This guide details on how to integrate with LinkedIn's Jobs Posting API.

The below button will take you to LinkedIn's Postman's workspace. Select the workspace with name `LinkedIn Talent Solutions`. You will find the `Job Posting` API collection in it. Learn more on our [Development Tools](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/api-development-tools?view=li-lts-2026-04) page.

[![Try in Postman](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/media/postman-button.png?view=li-lts-2026-04)](https://www.postman.com/linkedin-developer-apis?tab=workspaces)

[Section titled: Job Posting Legal Requirement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#job-posting-legal-requirement)

## Job Posting Legal Requirement

Note

- The use of these APIs is restricted to those developers approved by LinkedIn. Please reach out to your LinkedIn Relationship Manager or Business Development contact as you will need to meet certain criteria and sign an API agreement with data restrictions in order to use this integration.
- If you are not yet a LinkedIn Talent Solutions Partner, please complete the [LinkedIn Talent Solutions Partner Request Form.](https://business.linkedin.com/talent-solutions/ats-partners/partner-application)

In addition to any restrictions or obligations contained in a signed API agreement, partner:

- Acknowledges that LinkedIn acts as a passive conduit for the online distribution and publication of job listings and LinkedIn is not responsible for screening or monitoring job listings. Jobs posted to the LinkedIn Service (including via the LinkedIn APIs) may be posted only for lawful purposes by individuals and employers seeking employees. The LinkedIn APIs may not be used to post job listings that violate the restrictions included in the [LinkedIn Jobs Terms and Conditions](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/jobs-terms-conditions)
- Will ensure that its customers agree to the [LinkedIn Jobs Terms and Conditions](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/jobs-terms-conditions) prior to posting any jobs to the LinkedIn Service via partner’s application and shall have a method of keeping track of which of its customers have agreed to the [LinkedIn Jobs Terms and Conditions](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/jobs-terms-conditions) and when, and shall furnish such information to LinkedIn upon request
- Shall not market any job listings to be distributed via LinkedIn or its syndication network as a "free way to post jobs to LinkedIn" or anything substantially similar in any marketing or sales materials
- Acknowledges that in some cases, we may require certain types of jobs to be promoted on LinkedIn. Jobs that require promotion may include jobs by companies with generic names (such as “Confidential Company”). These limits are designed to prevent abuse, improve product quality, and increase transparency while ensuring that job seekers have access to the best possible opportunities. Please note that LinkedIn reserves the right to require promotion of jobs.

[Section titled: Development Milestones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#development-milestones)

## Development Milestones

[Section titled: Request Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#request-access)

### Request Access

Before beginning development, you will need to be provisioned access to test resources, and your API applications will have to be enabled to access the job posting API endpoints. You can request access by completing the following steps:

[Create API applications](https://www.linkedin.com/developer/apps) for the integration. You may create two API applications per integration - one for production, and another for development and testing. Please contact your LinkedIn Business Development point of contact and request to fill out the Partner Onboarding Form.

After the above steps, you are guided with test environment details that can be consumed for your development and testing. In order to test these APIs we will set up test organization which you can use to create and update test jobs. Please note that any jobs created to this page will be frequently closed and you should expect jobs created to this test organization to be short-lived.

[Section titled: Begin Development](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#begin-development)

### Begin Development

Once your application is configured, you may begin making API requests and testing the integration.

In order to post jobs on behalf of customers, you may need to create a child API Key. Refer to [Create and Configure Customer Application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#create-and-configure-customer-applications) to know the steps. LinkedIn's Job Posting API follows [Rest.li](https://linkedin.github.io/rest.li/spec/protocol#pagination-support) standards and requires [OAuth](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/client-credentials-flow?view=li-lts-2026-04). To learn more about Job Posting API, refer to [Sync Basic or Promoted Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-04).

You can post any of the below two job categories:

- **Basic Jobs** \- These are job posts aggregated on LinkedIn to create a comprehensive job-seeking experience for LinkedIn members. These jobs receive limited active promotion to members as compared to jobs posted in Job Slots (paid jobs). To post basic jobs refer to:

  - [Job Postings API Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-04) and [Create Basic Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/create-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-04#sample-request-for-basic-jobs)
  - [Foundation Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04)
- **Promoted Jobs** \- These are jobs posted in Job Slots as paid jobs. For customers with paid job slots, the API allows posting jobs directly into their Job Slots. To post promoted jobs refer to:

  - [Job Postings API Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-04) and [Create Promoted Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/create-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-04#sample-request-for-promoted-jobs)
  - [Foundation Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04) and [Promoted Jobs Extension Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04#promoted-jobs-extension-schema)

If you are an Apply Connect partner then you can use Job Posting API to also enable onsite apply. To create Apply Connect jobs refer to

- [Job Postings API Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-04) and [Create Apply Connect Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-connect/create-apply-connect-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-04)
- [Foundation Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04), [Apply Connect Extension Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04#apply-connect-extension-schema) and [OnsiteApplyConfiguration Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-connect/onsite-apply-configuration-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04)

[Section titled: Create and Configure Customer Applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#create-and-configure-customer-applications)

### Create and Configure Customer Applications

If you are a LinkedIn Partner (for example, Applicant Tracking System or Job Distributor) implementing Job Posting for multiple customers, please follow below steps to complete the Job Posting Integration.

1. Create and configure a customer(child) application for posting jobs on behalf of customer. The [Provisioning API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/middleware-platform/provisioning-api?view=li-lts-2026-04) allows you to create API keys for each of your customers using the parent application provisioned by LinkedIn
2. Once you have created customer application, you will need to store the `API Key` (client id for the customer application created by [Provisioning API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/middleware-platform/provisioning-api?view=li-lts-2026-04)) and a LinkedIn Developer Application id for each of your customers. You should also persist the companyID (and contractID for [Promoted Jobs Extension Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-04#promoted-jobs-extension-schema)) as provided by the customers when opting for posting jobs on LinkedIn
3. For existing customers of [Recruiter System Connect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/recruiter-system-connect?view=li-lts-2026-04), [Apply with LinkedIn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-with-linkedin/apply-with-linkedin?view=li-lts-2026-04) or [Apply Connect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-connect/apply-connect-overview?view=li-lts-2026-04) you will be using their existing customer API keys

Important

We expect partners to create only one application per customer account on your platform and use it to make all API calls such as Job Postings, RSC and Apply Connect. The customer account and its corresponsding application created via [Provisioning API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/middleware-platform/provisioning-api?view=li-lts-2026-04) should strictly have 1:1 mapping.

[Section titled: ATS Customer Onboarding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#ats-customer-onboarding)

### ATS Customer Onboarding

In order to enable Job Posting for a Recruiter customer, your application requires implementing an onboarding widget to collect below essential details to post a job.

Expand table

| Field | Note |
| --- | --- |
| organizationId | The LinkedIn company page ID of LinkedIn Recruiter customer |
| contractId | The contract ID of LinkedIn Recruiter customer. This is required only for posting paid jobs |

Below Help Article links can be shared to help customers find their Contract and Company ID:

1. For [Company ID](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a415420) refer to this help center
2. For [Contract ID](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/74336/finding-your-recruiter-contract-id?lang=en%3E) refer to this help center

Note

- The value of `integrationContext` field will be urn:li:organization:"organizationId"
- For Recruiter System Connect customers, `integrationContext` is provided by ATS customer onboarding widget. To know more, refer to [Recruiter System Connect's Customer OnBoarding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-customer-configuration?view=li-lts-2026-04)
- For others, the value of `integrationContext` field can be constructed manually if the customer provides value for `organizationId`. In absence of this value, provide the company information via `companyName` field
- Contract ID field is mandatory for [Premium job postings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/premium-job-posting?view=li-lts-2026-04)

Note

- The value of `company` field will be urn:li:company:{company\_id}"
- For Recruiter System Connect customers, `company` is provided by ATS customer onboarding widget. To know more, refer to [Recruiter System Connect's Customer OnBoarding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-customer-configuration?view=li-lts-2026-04)
- For others, the value of `company` field can be constructed manually if the customer provides value for `companyId`. In absence of this value, provide the company information via `companyName` field
- Contract ID field is mandatory for [Premium job postings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/premium-job-posting?view=li-lts-2026-04)

[Section titled: View Job Posting on LinkedIn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#view-job-posting-on-linkedin)

### View Job Posting on LinkedIn

When a customer posts a job on clients or ATS systems which are integrated with the Job Posting API, the job is published on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/jobs) and is associated company page on LinkedIn. It is similar to manually posting jobs in [New Recruiter and Jobs](https://business.linkedin.com/talent-solutions/learning-hub/new-recruiter-and-jobs#all)

![Company Page](https://content.linkedin.com/content/dam/developer/global/en_US/site/img/LTSImages/companyPage.png)![Job Description](https://content.linkedin.com/content/dam/developer/global/en_US/site/img/LTSImages/jobDescription.png)

[Section titled: Frequently Asked Questions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#frequently-asked-questions)

## Frequently Asked Questions

# API Overview

Feedback

Summarize this article for me


The LinkedIn's Job Posting API allows members to automatically post jobs to LinkedIn from their Applicant Tracking System (ATS), instead of manually posting using the website. This API enables partners to post and manage lifecycle for both **basic** or **promoted** jobs. The promoted jobs via API get promoted directly to paid job slots of LinkedIn Recruiter customers. Not all partners have the capability to post promoted jobs. To request for access, please reach out to your LinkedIn Business Development point of contact.

Note

If you are not yet a LinkedIn Talent Solutions Partner, please complete the [LinkedIn Talent Solutions Partner Request Form](https://business.linkedin.com/talent-solutions/ats-partners/partner-application)

Note

Please note that in some cases, we may require certain types of jobs to be promoted on LinkedIn. Jobs that require promotion may include jobs by companies with generic names (such as “Confidential Company”) or jobs from search and staffing companies. These limits are designed to prevent abuse, improve product quality, and increase transparency while ensuring that job seekers have access to the best possible opportunities. Please note that LinkedIn reserves the right to require promotion of jobs.

Note

The latest API version is **202604**. Use this version in the `LinkedIn-Version` header for all API requests to access the most recent features and improvements.

[Section titled: Job Posting API Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#job-posting-api-schema)

## Job Posting API Schema

In order to publish a job, you need to construct the request body with all required fields. The more information your application can provide, the more candidates can be reached to satisfy customers’ needs. To post basic jobs, refer to [**Foundation schema**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-03#foundation-schema). To enable advanced features on job posting, refer to [**Extension schema**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-03#promoted-jobs-extension-schema)

Important

For a given customer, when their first job is sent via the SJP API, all the customer’s open, public jobs should be sent via API. All future public jobs should also be sent via API.

[Section titled: Job Posting Operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#job-posting-operations)

## Job Posting Operations

Listed below are the four job posting operations supported by LinkedIn:

1. Create
2. Close
3. Update
4. Renew

Note

- For all the above operations, value for `jobPostingOperationType` field in [API schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-03) determines the operation to be performed.
- For example, use `jobPostingOperationType` as `CREATE` in request body to create a job.

[Section titled: Post Jobs on LinkedIn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#post-jobs-on-linkedin)

## Post Jobs on LinkedIn

[Section titled: API Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#api-endpoint)

### API Endpoint

Use the following endpoint to submit a task to create, close, update, or renew one or more jobs asynchronously:

https

Copy

```https
POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/simpleJobPostings
```

https

Copy

```https
POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/simpleJobPostings
```

[Section titled: API Authorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#api-authorization)

### API Authorization

All requests below require access tokens obtained via the [OAuth2.0 Client Credentials flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/client-credentials-flow?view=li-lts-2026-03).

Important

We strongly recommend to use same access token for all concurrent and consecutive calls. An access token has a lifespan of 30 mins. Only on expiry of the existing token, new token should be generated.

[Section titled: API Throttling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#api-throttling)

### API Throttling

Expand table

| Throttle Limits | Requests Per Day (UTC) | Records Per Minute | Records Per Day |

| Application maximum | 100,000 | 2,000 (applicable only for Promoted jobs) | 60,000 (applicable only for Promoted jobs) |

Refer to the below sections for sample requests and responses for each operation type.

[Section titled: Sample Request Body](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#sample-request-body)

### Sample Request Body

We have provided below wiki pages to help with API request samples as well as error guide tables based on the following job posting operation type:

- [Create Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/create-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-03)
- [Update and Renew Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/update-renew-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-03)
- [Close Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/close-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-03)

[Section titled: Continue RSC Development](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-03#continue-rsc-development)

[Section titled: Foundation Schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-03#foundation-schema) ## Foundation Schema The schema below includes attributes required for posting jobs on LinkedIn. The foundation schema represents the core schema that has to be implemented irrespective of integration type. The partner needs to implement the Foundation schema and can also build any extension schema(s) which are defined in the topics below. Expand table | Field | Description | Type | Required | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | integrationContext | Represents the unique identifier of the company page on LinkedIn for which this job is posted. Must be in the format urn:li:organization:{ [company\_id](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a415420)} for example, `urn:li:organization:1234`. If the company is a LinkedIn customer with access to the [onboarding widget](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-connect/create-configure-customer-application?view=li-lts-2026-03), then this field must be used to identify the company, else use companyName field | URN | `integrationContext` is a recommended field and must be provided to ensure job postings get associated with correct company page. Provide companyName field value only if you cannot provide value for this field. However, this does not guarantee a 100% accurate match with LinkedIn company page | | companyApplyUrl | URL for applicants to apply for the jobs | String | Yes | | externalJobPostingId | Represents unique job id within the partner system. Do not send an empty or null string for this field. The maximum allowed length is 75 characters | String | Yes | | jobPostingOperationType | Represents the operation on the job posting. Available operation options are: CREATE, UPDATE, RENEW, CLOSE | String | Yes | | title | Represents the title of the job posting that will be published. Character limit: 200 | String | Yes | | description | Represents the job description including the job basic information, responsibility and so on. Character limit: 100 ~ 25,000, limited set of [HTML tags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-03#html-tags) accepted, non-support HTML tags will be ignored. | String | Yes | | listedAt | Represents initial date the job posting was added into the application tracking system. The date is epoch timestamp in milliseconds (UTC) and should not be a future time | Integer | Yes | | location | Represents the geographic location of the job position to hire. Please use one of the below recommended formats:
- "CITY, STATE, COUNTRY"
- "CITY, STATE"
- "CITY, PROVINCE"
- "CITY, COUNTRY"
- "POSTALCODE, COUNTRYCODE"
- "COUNTRY" (accepted only for Remote jobs)
- "COUNTRY CLUSTER" (accepted only for Remote jobs)
To know more about

You can try changing directories. # Create Apply Connect jobs - API overview Feedback Summarize this article for me As a partner, you can integrate with Apply Connect using the Job Posting API. This API helps you create and manage Apply Connect jobs on LinkedIn for your customers. LinkedIn members can view these job postings and apply to them directly on the platform. Additionally, using this API, you can collect job applications directly on your website through webhooks. However, Apply Connect jobs require additional fields because LinkedIn hosts the application experience and delivers applications to partners, unlike PJP or RSC jobs. Important - Continue to maintain XML Feeds if you have an Apply Connect integration. - Send all public jobs to LinkedIn only through this API for your Apply Connect customers. - Ensure job IDs (`externalJobPostingId` or `companyJobCode`) match across XML feeds, career sites, and API jobs. - Maintain data parity by syncing all available job data from external career sites and XML feeds. - Send all open, public jobs through the API once you send one job through the API. Note LinkedIn will notify you when all customers have migrated to the API and when to disable XML Feeds (typically around 3 months after general access). [Section titled: Legal requirements for the API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/apply-connect/create-apply-connect-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-04&tabs=http#legal-requirements-for-the-api) ## Legal requirements for the API **Job Posting legal requirements** - The use of these APIs is restricted to those developers approved by LinkedIn. The LinkedIn APIs may not be used to post job listings that violate the restrictions included in the [LinkedIn Jobs Terms and Conditions](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/jobs-terms-conditions) - Will ensure that its customers agree to the [LinkedIn Jobs Terms and Conditions](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/jobs-terms-conditions) prior to posting any jobs to the LinkedIn Service via partner’s application and shall have a method of keeping track of which of its customers have agreed to the [LinkedIn Jobs Terms and Conditions](https://www.linkedin.com/legal/jobs-terms-conditions) and when, and shall furnish such information to LinkedIn upon request - Shall not market any job listings to be distributed via LinkedIn or its syndication network as a "free way to post jobs to LinkedIn" or anything substantially similar in any marketing or sales materials - Acknowledges that in some cases, LinkedIn may require certain types of jobs to be promoted on LinkedIn. These limits are designed to prevent abuse, improve product quality, and increase transparency while ensuring that job seekers have access to the best possible opportunities. LinkedIn reserves the right to require promotion of jobs. This is an asynchronous API and you will receive a task id which you can use to see the status of the job, verify whether it successfully posted to LinkedIn, or see if there was an error during creation and view any details about the error. The API also provides many additional fields to post, which would be used for job recommendation. The more information your application can provide, the more candidates can be reached to satisfy customers’ needs. See [this page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema?view=li-lts-2026-03) for full field schema information. [Section titled: Authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-premium-api-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-03#authentication) ### Authentication All requests below require access tokens obtained via the [OAuth 2 Client Credentials flow.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/client-credentials-flow?view=li-lts-2026-03&%3Fcontext=linkedin%2Ftalent%2Fcontext) [Section titled: Throttling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-premium-api-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-03#throttling) ### Throttling Expand table | Throttle Limits | Requests Per Day (UTC) | Records Per Minute | Records Per Day | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Application maximum | 100,000 | 2,000 | 60,000 | [Section titled: Rest.li Concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-premium-api-jobs?view=li-lts-2026-03#restli-concepts) ### Rest.li Concepts APIs below are built on the top of LinkedIn REST framework [rest.li](http://rest.li/) , which are similar as standard REST APIs, but provide more rich features, like field projections, extended request methods etc. It’s highly recommended to read [these technical details](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/api-guide/concepts?view=li-lts-2026-03) before development. Feedback

Summarize this article for me


LinkedIn's Simple Job Posting API enables authorized third parties to post jobs directly to LinkedIn. This is an asynchronous API and you will receive a task id which you can use to see the status of the job, verify whether it successfully posted to LinkedIn, or see if there was an error during creation and view any details about the error.

These limits are designed to prevent abuse, improve product quality, and increase transparency while ensuring that job seekers have access to the best possible opportunities. Please note that LinkedIn reserves the right to require promotion of jobs.

# Job Requisition API Migration Guide

Feedback

Summarize this article for me


LinkedIn has released a new API endpoint, `/jobRequisitions`, to replace the older `/simpleJobPostings` API for job requisitions. This update helps keep job postings and job requisitions separate. Earlier, both were managed using the same API.

As RSC partners, you are required to migrate to the new `/jobRequisitions` endpoint by _July 31, 2027_. Go through the following sections to learn more about the endpoint updates and migration guidelines.

Note

The latest API version is **202604**. Use this version in the `LinkedIn-Version` header for all API requests to access the most recent features and improvements.

[Section titled: Job posting versus job requisition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#job-posting-versus-job-requisition)

## Job posting versus job requisition

- **Job posting**: A job ad that is shown to candidates on LinkedIn or other websites.
- **Job requisition**: An internal request used by recruiters or hiring managers to fill a job. It includes information like budget, job status, and approval details.

The following table summarizes the differences between job postings and job requisitions:

Expand table

| Aspect | Job posting | Job requisition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audience | External candidates | Internal recruiters/hiring managers |
| Purpose | Attract job seekers | Request and manage hiring needs |
| Visibility | Public job boards | LinkedIn Recruiter (1CE) |

[Section titled: Benefits of the separate APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#benefits-of-the-separate-apis)

## Benefits of the separate APIs

Jobs used for [One Click Export](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-faq?view=li-lts-2026-03#product-functionality-one-click-export) (1CE) function more like internal job requisitions and are not meant to be seen by the public on LinkedIn or other websites. Separating the APIs will

- To better serve RSC users' preference to manage sourcing at the Job Requisitions level and to 1CE candidates directly to requisitions.
- To better capture this workflow intent and prepare for future integration enhancements.

To streamline LinkedIn's job posting APIs and align with how RSC partners manage sourcing, all RSC partners must migrate from the previous Job Posting API to the new Job Requisitions API. Posting RSC (private) jobs using Job Posting API will not be supported in the new versioned APIs. Use the versioned Job Requisition API instead.

[Section titled: Changes after switching APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#changes-after-switching-apis)

## Changes after switching APIs

[Section titled: For One Click Export (1CE)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#for-one-click-export-1ce)

#### For One Click Export (1CE)

- Old requisitions (private jobs) using `/simpleJobPostings` will still show up in the 1CE dropdown.
- New requisitions using `/jobRequisitions` will also show up in the 1CE dropdown.
- When the new `externalJobRequisitionId` field value matches the old `externalJobPostingId`, only the Job Requisition will be shown and not the old Job Posting record. This keeps the requisition as one entry in the dropdown instead of creating duplicates.

[Section titled: For ATS applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#for-ats-applications)

#### For ATS applications

- ATS applications created with the old API will still appear in LinkedIn Recruiter.
- New or updated ATS applications will also appear, as long as they are linked to a job requisition/old private job posting using `externalJobRequisitionId`.

[Section titled: Field mapping: /simpleJobPostings versus /jobRequisitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#field-mapping-simplejobpostings-versus-jobrequisitions)

## Field mapping: `/simpleJobPostings` versus `/jobRequisitions`

The following table compares the fields in the old and new APIs, and highlights new fields introduced in the `/jobRequisitions` API.

Expand table

| Field in `/simpleJobPostings` | Field in `/jobRequisitions` | New Field? | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `externalJobPostingId` | `externalJobRequisitionId` | ✅ | Unique identifier for the job requisition. |
| `jobPostingOperationType` | `requisitionStatus` | ✅ | Current status of the job—either `OPEN` or `CLOSED`. |
| `accessRestricted` (extension schema) | `accessRestricted` | – | Marks the job as private (ACL-protected) or public. |
| `title` | `title` | – | Job title shown on LinkedIn. |
| `description` | `description` | – | Description of the job role and responsibilities. |
| `location` | `locations` | – | One or more geographic job locations. |
| `skillsDescription` | `basicSkills` | ✅ | Must-have skills and experience. |
| _Not available_ | `preferredSkills` | ✅ | Nice-to-have skills in addition to basic skills. |
| `categories` | `categories` | – | Tags that describe the job function or domain. |
| `workplaceTypes` | `workplaceTypes` | – | Work setting—Remote, On-site, or Hybrid. |
| `industries` | `industries` | – | URNs representing relevant industries. |
| _Not available_ | `compensation` | ✅ | Salary or wage details for the job. |
| `experienceLevel` | `experienceLevel` | – | Level of experience required (e.g., Internship, Senior). |
| `employmentStatus` | `employmentStatus` | – | Type of employment—Full-time, Part-time, etc. |
| _Not available_ | `requisitionType` | ✅ | Type of requisition—`STANDARD` or `EVERGREEN`. `EVERGREEN` must not include a parent requisition ID. |
| `requisitionOwnerFirstName`, `requisitionOwnerLastName`, `requisitionOwnerEmail` | `owners` | – | Requisition owners with contact details. |
| _Not available_ | `numberOfOpenings` | ✅ | Total number of positions to be filled. |
| _Not available_ | `parentRequisitionId` | ✅ | ID of the parent requisition for evergreen hiring model. |
| _Not available_ | `externalCreatedAt` | ✅ | Time when the job was created in the partner system (epoch UTC). |
| _Not available_ | `externalLastModifiedAt` | ✅ | Time when the job was last updated in the partner system (epoch UTC). |
| _Not available_ | `targetedStartAt` | ✅ | Preferred start date for candidates (epoch time, UTC). |
| _Not available_ | `hiredCount` | ✅ | Number of candidates hired for this requisition. |

[Section titled: API request comparison](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#api-request-comparison)

## API request comparison

The differences between old and new API request bodies are the following:

[Section titled: Old API: /simpleJobPostings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#old-api-simplejobpostings)

### Old API: `/simpleJobPostings`

This endpoint supported creating and syncing job postings for public listings.

Bash

Copy

```bash
curl --location 'https://api.linkedin.com/v2/simpleJobPostings' \
--header 'x-restli-method: batch_create' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}' \
--data-raw '{
  "elements": [\
    {\
      "title": "Example Job",\
      ...\
    }\
  ]
}'
```

## Migration guidelines

By **July 31, 2027**, ensure to

- use the `/jobRequisitions` API to create or update all old and new job requisitions.
- submit all new or updated ATS applications via the latest version of the `atsApplications` API, including the corresponding job requisition ID.
- discontinue all traffic to unversioned `atsApplications` and `simpleJobPostings` endpoints for job requisitions.

Follow the guidelines below to use the appropriate endpoints for creating, updating, and syncing different jobs.

[Section titled: Creating job requisitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#creating-job-requisitions)

### Creating job requisitions

- To create a new job requisition in RSC 1CE, use the `/jobRequisitions` endpoint to submit the job details.
- To define the template stages that all job applications can progress through, send a stage update using the `/jobRequisitionStage` endpoint.

[Section titled: Updating job requisitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#updating-job-requisitions)

### Updating job requisitions

- To update an existing job, use the `/jobRequisitions` endpoint to submit the revised job requisition details.
- To specify the application stages for a job requisition, include the relevant stages via the `/jobRequisitionStage` endpoint when creating or updating the job requisition.

[Section titled: Syncing ATS applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#syncing-ats-applications)

### Syncing ATS applications

- To create a new application, include the required `atsJobRequisitionId` field and post the related job using the `/jobRequisitions` endpoint (`atsJobRequisitionId` is mandatory for any new atsApplication record).
- For detailed information on syncing ATS applications, refer to [Sync Applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/middleware-platform/sync-applications?view=li-lts-2026-03).

[Section titled: Maintaining existing jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#maintaining-existing-jobs)

### Maintaining existing jobs

- Jobs previously posted via `/simpleJobPostings` remain visible in RSC 1CE.
- To update those jobs using `/jobRequisitions`, ensure the `externalJobRequisitionId` matches the old `externalJobPostingId`.

[Section titled: Handling public job posts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#handling-public-job-posts)

### Handling public job posts

- For job requisition (private) jobs syncing, use `/jobRequisitions`. For public job syncing, use versioned `/simpleJobPostings` endpoint.
- Once you begin private job syncing via `/jobRequisitions`, do not use the old endpoint `/simpleJobPostings` for any private/internal job sync after migration.

[Section titled: Handling One Click Export](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#handling-one-click-export)

### Handling One Click Export

- Use the `/exportedCandidate` endpoint to retrieve exported candidates. For detailed information, see [Retrieve Exported Candidates Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/retrieve-exported-candidates?view=li-lts-2026-03). In the response, the values of the `referenceEntityType` field will be "REQUISITION" and the `referenceEntityId` will be the job requisition ID that was used to export the candidate.

[Section titled: Handling ACL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/recruiter-system-connect/rsc-migration-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03#handling-acl)

### Handling ACL

- To create a new ACL group, retrieve, update, or delete an existing ACL group, use `/entityAcls` with parameter `entityType=JOB_REQUISITION`.
- To create, retrieve, update, or delete existing ACL assignees, use `/entityAclAssignees`.

# Job Posting Overview

Feedback

Summarize this article for me


Jobs that are already created externally on ATS, company site, or job board can be automatically ingested by LinkedIn. LinkedIn provides various solutions to ingest such jobs to our customers, partner ATSs' and Job Distributors.

[Section titled: Ingesting Jobs on LinkedIn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/job-posting-overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#ingesting-jobs-on-linkedin)

## Ingesting Jobs on LinkedIn

Below are the different solutions for customers or partners to ingest jobs on LinkedIn:

- **API** \- LinkedIn's Job Posting API enables authorized third parties, such as clients, ATS systems, and job distributors, to post jobs directly to LinkedIn on behalf of customers. Please refer to [Job Posting API Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/overview?view=li-lts-2026-04) for more information.

- **XML Feeds** \- When your customer creates a job in your system, the XML feed sends jobs to LinkedIn. These XML feeds contain the job posting information that helps facilitate creating a job that displays on LinkedIn. Please refer to [XML Feeds Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds?view=li-lts-2026-04) for more information.


Note

To avoid duplication, use either of the above solutions to ingest jobs on LinkedIn. Refer to [FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/job-posting-faq?view=li-lts-2026-04) to know more.

[Section titled: Job Posting Categories](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/job-posting-overview?view=li-lts-2026-04#job-posting-categories)

## Job Posting Categories

The following two job categories broadly define the ways to post jobs in LinkedIn:

- **Basic Jobs** \- These are free job posts gathered by LinkedIn from external sources such as ATS, job boards, distributors and aggregators across the web to create a comprehensive job-seeking experience for LinkedIn members. Basic jobs can be posted using [Job Postings API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-04) or [XML feeds](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds?view=li-lts-2026-04). For customers who purchased Job Slots, LinkedIn offers [Job Wrapping](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a412393) which allows job posters to prioritize specific ingested basic jobs to automatically promote into customer's job slots based on some tags or rules.

- **Promoted Jobs** \- These are paid job postings. You can directly post promoted jobs using [Job Postings API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/sync-job-postings?view=li-lts-2026-04). For customers with paid job slots, the API allows posting jobs directly into their job slots.
